description: Experience the quintessential flavors of India with this Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled recipe. Marinated in a rich blend of yogurt and aromatic spices, the chicken is cooked to smoky perfection over charcoal, resulting in incredibly tender and juicy meat with a beautiful charred exterior. This dish brings the authentic taste of a traditional tandoor oven right to your backyard grill.

ingredients.notes: whole chicken cut into 8 pieces or bone-in chicken thighs/drumsticks, deeply scored

instructions.title: Prepare the Chicken
instructions.text: Wash and pat dry the chicken pieces thoroughly. Make deep gashes on each piece to allow the marinade to penetrate.

instructions.title: First Marinade
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine ginger-garlic paste, lemon juice, salt, and Kashmiri red chili powder. Rub this mixture all over the chicken pieces, ensuring it gets into the gashes. Let it marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours in the refrigerator. This step helps tenderize the chicken.

instructions.title: Second Marinade
instructions.text: In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, coriander powder, cumin powder, garam masala, turmeric powder, black pepper, and mustard oil. Add a few drops of red food color if desired. Mix well until smooth.

instructions.title: Combine and Marinate
instructions.text: Add the chicken from the first marinade to the second yogurt-spice mixture. Ensure every piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for a minimum of 4 hours, or preferably overnight, for best flavor and tenderness.

instructions.title: Prepare the Grill
instructions.text: Set up your charcoal grill for direct medium-high heat. Once the coals are hot and covered with a light gray ash, clean the grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.

instructions.title: Grill the Chicken
instructions.text: Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the hot coals. Cook for 25-35 minutes, turning every 5-7 minutes to ensure even cooking and charring. Baste occasionally with butter or oil during the last 10-15 minutes of cooking. The chicken is done when internal temperature reaches 165F (74C) and juices run clear.

instructions.title: Rest and Serve
instructions.text: Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for a few minutes. Sprinkle with chaat masala if desired, garnish with fresh cilantro and lemon wedges. Serve hot with mint chutney, onion rings, or naan bread.

tips: For truly authentic flavor, use full-fat Greek yogurt as it is thicker and adheres better to the chicken, preventing the marinade from dripping off during grilling.
Deeply scoring the chicken pieces is crucial for the marinade to penetrate and flavor the meat thoroughly, ensuring a tender and juicy result.
Do not skip the overnight marination; it significantly enhances the flavor and tenderness of the Tandoori Chicken, making it incredibly succulent.
article:
Embark on a culinary journey to the heart of India, where vibrant spices meet the smoky embrace of a charcoal grill. Tandoori Chicken, a global superstar among Indian dinner recipes, is a dish that captivates with its striking color, aromatic flavors, and succulent texture. While traditionally cooked in a clay tandoor oven, recreating that magic at home is entirely possible and incredibly rewarding, especially when you master the art of Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled. This method infuses the chicken with an irresistible smoky depth that elevates it from a simple meal to an unforgettable feast.

## What is Tandoori Chicken?

Tandoori Chicken is a classic Indian dish originating from the Punjab region, now famously enjoyed worldwide. It consists of chicken pieces, usually bone-in and skinless, marinated in a mixture of yogurt and a potent blend of spices before being cooked at high heat. The name "tandoori" refers to the tandoor, a cylindrical clay oven used for cooking and baking in parts of Asia. This unique oven imparts a distinct smoky flavor and ensures the chicken cooks evenly, developing a beautifully charred exterior while remaining incredibly juicy inside. The signature red-orange hue often associated with Tandoori Chicken comes from a combination of Kashmiri red chili powder and, sometimes, a touch of food coloring, making it as visually appealing as it is delicious.

## Why Charcoal Grill Your Tandoori Chicken?

While modern kitchens offer conveniences like oven baking or gas grilling, opting for a charcoal grill to prepare your Tandoori Chicken is a game-changer. The primary reason lies in the unparalleled flavor profile. Charcoal grilling imparts a deep, smoky aroma and taste that simply cannot be replicated by other methods. As the chicken fat drips onto the hot coals, it creates flavorful smoke that permeates the meat, adding layers of complexity to the marinade's spices. This process results in a beautifully charred exterior, crispy in parts, while locking in the juices to keep the chicken wonderfully tender and moist. For an authentic experience that truly captures the essence of traditional Indian cooking, Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is the superior choice for any Indian dinner recipes spread, offering a rustic charm and an explosion of flavors that will impress even the most discerning palate.

## Ingredients You'll Need

To create your own mouth-watering Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled, gather these essential ingredients:

*   **For the Chicken:**
    *   2-3 lbs chicken pieces (thighs, drumsticks, or a whole cut-up chicken), bone-in, skinless
    *   2 tablespoons lemon juice
    *   1 teaspoon salt
*   **For the Marinade:**
    *   1 cup plain full-fat yogurt (Greek yogurt can be used, but thin with a little water)
    *   2 tablespoons ginger-garlic paste
    *   1 tablespoon Kashmiri red chili powder (for color and mild heat)
    *   1 teaspoon turmeric powder
    *   1 teaspoon ground cumin
    *   1 teaspoon ground coriander
    *   1 teaspoon garam masala
    *   1/2 teaspoon black pepper
    *   1/4 teaspoon cayenne pepper (optional, for extra heat)
    *   2 tablespoons mustard oil (or any vegetable oil)
    *   1/2 teaspoon red food coloring (optional, for traditional vibrant color)

## Step-by-Step Instructions for Charcoal Grilled Tandoori Chicken

Follow these steps to create perfectly Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled:

1.  **Prepare the Chicken:** Rinse the chicken pieces thoroughly and pat them dry with paper towels. Using a sharp knife, make 2-3 deep slits into each chicken piece. This allows the marinade to penetrate deeply, ensuring maximum flavor.
2.  **First Marinade:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with lemon juice and 1 teaspoon of salt. Rub it all over the chicken, making sure the lemon juice gets into the slits. Let it sit for 15-20 minutes at room temperature. This step tenderizes the chicken and helps the second marinade adhere better.
3.  **Second Marinade:** In a separate bowl, whisk together the yogurt, ginger-garlic paste, Kashmiri red chili powder, turmeric, cumin, coriander, garam masala, black pepper, cayenne (if using), mustard oil, and red food coloring (if using). Mix until smooth and well combined.
4.  **Marinate the Chicken:** Add the chicken pieces to the yogurt-spice mixture, ensuring each piece is thoroughly coated. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, or preferably overnight (12-24 hours) for the best flavor penetration. The longer the marination, the more flavorful and tender your chicken will be.
5.  **Prepare the Grill:** About 30-45 minutes before grilling, prepare your charcoal grill. Arrange the hot coals to create both direct and indirect heat zones. You'll want a medium-high heat (around 375-400°F or 190-200°C). Clean the grill grates and lightly oil them to prevent sticking.
6.  **Grill the Chicken:** Place the marinated chicken pieces directly over the medium-high heat. Sear for 2-3 minutes per side to get a nice char. Then, move the chicken to the indirect heat zone to cook through, closing the lid. Cook for 20-30 minutes, turning occasionally, until the internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C) when measured with a meat thermometer. For extra flavor, you can baste with any leftover marinade during the last 10 minutes of cooking (ensure it's cooked through afterwards).
7.  **Rest and Serve:** Once cooked, remove the Tandoori Chicken from the grill and let it rest for 5-10 minutes. This allows the juices to redistribute, ensuring a more tender and flavorful chicken.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

Achieving perfect Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled requires a few expert touches:

*   **Quality Chicken:** Use fresh, good-quality chicken. Bone-in, skinless chicken pieces like thighs and drumsticks work best as they stay moist and flavorful.
*   **Full-Fat Yogurt:** Full-fat yogurt creates a richer marinade that adheres better and helps tenderize the chicken without making it watery.
*   **Deep Scoring:** Don't be shy with the slits. Deeper cuts allow the marinade to truly infuse the meat.
*   **Long Marination is Key:** This cannot be stressed enough. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Don't Overcrowd the Grill:** Cook in batches if necessary. Overcrowding lowers the grill temperature and can lead to uneven cooking.
*   **Control Your Heat:** Start with direct heat for charring, then move to indirect heat for thorough cooking. This prevents burning the exterior before the interior is done.
*   **Use a Meat Thermometer:** This is the most reliable way to ensure your chicken is cooked to a safe internal temperature of 165°F (74°C) without overcooking and drying it out.
*   **Rest the Chicken:** Always rest the chicken for a few minutes after grilling. It makes a significant difference in juiciness.

## Serving Suggestions

Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is a versatile dish that can be the star of your Indian dinner recipes or part of a larger spread. It's traditionally served hot, garnished with fresh cilantro and a squeeze of lemon juice.

*   **Bread:** Pair it with warm naan bread, roti, or paratha to scoop up the delicious flavors.
*   **Chutney:** A cooling mint chutney or a spicy green chili chutney makes an excellent accompaniment.
*   **Salad:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) provides a refreshing contrast.
*   **Rice:** Basmati rice, jeera rice (cumin rice), or a mild vegetable pulao can complete the meal.
*   **Onions:** Thinly sliced red onions, sometimes marinated in a little vinegar, add a nice bite.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Tandoori Chicken is a masterpiece, feel free to experiment:

*   **Chicken Cuts:** Boneless chicken thighs or breast can be used, but adjust grilling time as they cook faster.
*   **Vegetarian Options:** The same marinade works wonderfully for paneer (Indian cheese), cauliflower florets, mushrooms, or bell peppers, creating delicious vegetarian tandoori skewers.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder or cayenne to suit your preference for heat.
*   **Oil:** While mustard oil adds an authentic pungent note, any neutral-flavored vegetable oil like canola or sunflower oil can be used.
*   **Alternative Cooking Methods:** If charcoal grilling isn't an option, you can achieve good results in a hot oven (400°F/200°C) or on a gas grill, though you'll miss the distinct smoky flavor that Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled offers.

Tandoori Chicken Charcoal Grilled is more than just a meal; it's an experience. The rich history, the vibrant spices, and the irresistible smoky char come together to create a dish that is truly a jewel in the crown of Indian dinner recipes. With a little preparation and these detailed steps, you can bring the authentic flavors of India right to your backyard grill. Enjoy the process, and savor every tender, smoky bite!
